clue.text: Plain if ornamental sort of grass

definitions.meaning: a plain is a wide flat treeless expanse, like the grasslands of South America
a tall feathery grass grown in gardens for its plumes

explanation.definitionFit: The South American grasslands give their name both to the open plain itself and to the tall plumed grass grown in gardens.

clue.text: What the unsuccessful are urged to try

definitions.text: What the unsuccessful are urged to try

parts.words: What the unsuccessful are urged to try
parts.note: the proverb tells those who fail at first to try, try once more

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'if at first you don't succeed, try, try ...' urges another attempt, so the word means once more.

clue.text: Accuracy in the abstract — very small matter

parts.note: an abstract is a summary of a text, also called a precis
an ion is a tiny charged particle of matter

explanation.surface: Someone praises the exactness of an abstract summary of minute physics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstract' looks like an adjective but is the noun, a summary or precis.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness and correctness are what accuracy means, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One direction on batting to leg-breaks

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
in cricket the side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: breaks tells us the letters of leg are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket note: one batsman facing leg-breaks, the spinning deliveries, runs in a single direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges the letters of the word leg. The surface is cricket: a leg-break is a spin bowler's delivery turning from the leg side, and a single is one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Single and one both mean a sole unit, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Hit an awkward situation in ""Moby Dick "'?

definitions.note: the definition is by example: the white whale has the feature, so the phrase points to a part of him

parts.note: a hit is a blow
to be in a hole is to be in trouble or an awkward spot

explanation.surface: A question about striking trouble in Melville's novel about the white whale.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a whale such as Moby Dick breathes through this nostril on top of its head, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales breathe and spout through a nostril on top of the head, which Melville's white whale would have.

clue.text: Vic's brakes rated faulty-they are a menace to fellow-motorists

definitions.text: they are a menace to fellow-motorists

indicators.note: faulty means the letters are wrongly arranged and must be put right

parts.note: the name Vic with its S kept as a letter for the shuffle

explanation.surface: Vic's brakes were judged defective, so he endangers other drivers on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' signals rearranging all fifteen letters of VICS BRAKES RATED. The answer means passengers who nag the driver, not drivers themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers who constantly give unwanted driving advice are a notorious nuisance to people at the wheel.

clue.text: Too fastidious concerning Mediterranean resort

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a quarrel over money
Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone is overly fussy about a holiday town on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too fussy or excessively particular is the sense of an old word for overly refined.

clue.text: Rustic used roundabout name for Sinai

annotationWithheld.why: Rustic used roundabout name for Sinai (5): HOREB looks like HOB (rustic) round RE, but no separate clue word gives RE; 'roundabout' would have to be both container indicator and RE
annotationWithheld.clue: Rustic used roundabout name for Sinai

clue.text: She takes in washing for the French strip joint

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the, so the French for 'the' gives these letters
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A woman doing laundry works at a French striptease club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'joint' link the pieces; 'strip joint' pretends to be a seedy club.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who washes clothes for a living, taking in other people's washing, is the classic description of a washerwoman.

clue.text: Crane shifted furniture outside a place of worship

indicators.note: outside means the furniture word goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

indicators.note: shifted says the letters of crane are moved around

explanation.surface: A lifting crane moves furniture out in front of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' scrambles the bird-like lifting machine's name, and 'outside' places the furniture around those scrambled letters. The tabernacle was the portable sanctuary of the Israelites.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent sanctuary in the Bible, and later a nonconformist chapel, is a building used for worship.

clue.text: Fish lost head in defeat

indicators.note: lost head means the first letter of the fish word is dropped

parts.note: a trout is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish lost its head while being beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A crushing defeat is called a rout, a synonym.

clue.text: Calls for letters in break — not right

indicators.note: break means the letters of the words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A demand for letters during a break from the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges LETTERS IN once 'not right' has removed its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To name or give a title to someone is to call them something, a synonym.

clue.text: Incorporeal diarist?

parts.note: something without a physical form has no flesh at all; the diarist is Mr Pooter of the Grossmiths' comic Diary of a ...

explanation.walkthrough: Charles Pooter is the fictional diarist of 'The Diary of a Nobody' (1892) by George and Weedon Grossmith.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance, punned as one with no physical form, is the title character of the Grossmiths' comic diary.

clue.text: Desert flower-bed ?

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river, so this is a river's bed in arid country

explanation.definitionFit: In arid lands a dry valley that becomes a river only in rainy seasons is a riverbed in the desert.

clue.text: Temptation on wheels ?

parts.note: the fruit of Eden's temptation loaded on a wheeled barrow

explanation.definitionFit: A barrow of fruit, Eve's tempting fruit on a wheeled cart; upsetting one means spoiling plans.

clue.text: Recognized a double century record by Edward

indicators.note: double asks for two copies of the century letter, one after the other

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century in cricket
an EP is an extended-play record
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward's score of two hundred has been officially acknowledged as a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double century' sounds like cricket but gives CC, two Roman hundreds.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to acknowledge or recognize it as valid.

clue.text: Gambler loses his head, becomes an embezzler

indicators.note: loses his head means the gambler word drops its first letter

parts.note: a speculator gambles on markets

explanation.surface: A gambler panics and turns to stealing from his firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses his head' pretends to mean panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who misappropriates public funds entrusted to him is a peculator, an embezzler.

clue.text: Sticker damaged in Crab Lane

indicators.note: damaged tells us the letters of the two words are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something sticky was broken in a street called Crab Lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges CRABLANE. 'Sticker' is a playful definition: the shellfish clings to rocks and hulls.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean fastens itself firmly to ship hulls and rocks, so it is something that sticks.

clue.text: Native returns pipe with an added note

indicators.note: returns means the whole sequence of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a drain is a pipe carrying waste water
PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A local man sends back a pipe with a note attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses DRAIN + A + PS as a whole, giving SPANIARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in Spain is a native of that country.

clue.text: Firm has shut up club

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A business has closed down its club.
explanation.walkthrough: A cosh is a British word for a short heavy bludgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A short heavy weapon for hitting people is a cudgel or club.

clue.text: Leather work on which we need money?

definitions.text: Leather work on which we need money?

parts.words: Leather work on which we need money?
parts.note: the upper leather parts of shoes; being on these means being penniless

explanation.walkthrough: To be 'on one's uppers' is a British idiom for being very poor, from shoes worn through to their tops.
explanation.definitionFit: The tops of shoes are leather, and the idiom of being down to them means being broke.

clue.text: Severe reproof given in some form ?

definitions.meaning: a sharp telling-off that teaches someone not to repeat a mistake
a school class is a form, where pupils are taught

explanation.definitionFit: A rebuke that teaches, and a period of teaching given to a school class or form.

clue.text: Chancy business for a cleaner

definitions.meaning: a sweepstake, a lottery-style bet on a race

explanation.definitionFit: A gamble in which stakes go to drawn tickets, and someone who clears soot from chimneys.

clue.text: Rude little devil Leo upset about something

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the next piece
upset says the letters of Leo are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: it can stand for an unspecified thing

explanation.surface: A naughty child bothers Leo about something, being discourteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the name Leo to OLE, and 'about' wraps that scramble round the pronoun for something. 'little devil' is a stock crossword phrase for a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking good manners, discourteous, is a synonym of rude.

clue.text: Medicine put in chest on ice

indicators.note: put in signals the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A remedy is stored in a cooler, kept chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through cheST ON ICe.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative medicine meant to invigorate is called this.

clue.text: Suit packed ?

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, and packed clothes go in a container; one word serves both

explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit is a legal action, and luggage for packed clothes is the same word.

clue.text: Girl demands mild in the Elephant's Head

parts.note: clement means mild, of weather

indicators.note: Head means only the first letter of the animal word is used

explanation.surface: A girl asks for a mild beer in a pub called the Elephant's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demands' and 'the' are link words. 'mild' pretends to be a British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, famous from the folk song 'Oh my darling'.

clue.text: Irish author and poet joins stage females

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
hens are female birds

explanation.surface: An Irish writer joins a troupe of actresses on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: James Stephens (1880-1950) was an Irish novelist and poet, author of 'The Crock of Gold'.
explanation.definitionFit: James Stephens was a Dublin novelist and poet.

clue.text: Trim the tree

definitions.meaning: trim as an adjective means neat and smart
a conifer of the pine family

explanation.definitionFit: Neat and smart in appearance, and a conifer with short needles.
